extracted.intended_audience: Researchers and administrators preparing NIAID multiproject (P- and U-series) grant applications
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for planning, writing, and submitting multiproject (P- and U-series) research grant applications to NIAID, including program structure, required components, review expectations, and electronic submission via ASSIST.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contact NIAID early
rubrics_metrics.description: While still in the planning stage, contact a program officer in the NIAID division that would support your work if funded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants are strongly encouraged to consult NIAID staff at least 10 weeks (15 weeks for P01s) before the application due date. Contacting staff helps determine if the proposed project meets Institute goals, provides input about using the multiproject approach, feedback on the research idea, and division-specific guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow NOFO instructions
rubrics_metrics.description: When you apply, follow all NIH and NIAID instructions for multiproject grants in the notice of funding opportunity (NOFO).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Read the announcement associated with the NOFO as it may have unique instructions that take precedence over others. Do not submit an application that proposes a clinical trial unless the NOFO explicitly states that it accepts clinical trials. If questions remain, contact the program officer listed in the announcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiproject grant core features
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiproject grants must have at least two interrelated research projects related to a theme, each capable of standing on its own scientific merit but complementing one another.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect collaboration and interaction among projects and investigators to achieve a common goal, synergy among projects, one grantee institution that is legally and financially responsible for funds, and support as needed for shared resources (cores) that provide services to at least two research projects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select appropriate activity code/opportunity type
rubrics_metrics.description: Choose the correct multiproject activity code (e.g., P01, P30, P50, U19, U54, UM2) or respond to an RFA/cooperative agreement as appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand differences: P01 is a program project headed by a PI (investigator-initiated P01s accepted by NIAID), P30 supports shared resources/cores, P50 is a specialized center, U19 requires substantial NIAID staff involvement, U54 supports research and development centers, UM2 supports large-scale centers with complex structures. Use the NOFO to decide which mechanism fits the project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple PI eligibility and rules
rubrics_metrics.description: For most NOFOs, you may submit a multiple PI application unless specified otherwise; check the NOFO for exceptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some NIAID opportunities don't offer a multiple PI option. Investigator-initiated P01s do not allow foreign investigators as PIs unless they are present in the U.S. on a visa. For multiple PI applications, make sure each PI is registered in eRA Commons and include a multi-PI plan if required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Option to submit component as separate R01
rubrics_metrics.description: You may simultaneously submit a component research project as a separate R01 application to maximize funding chances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The component project should be able to stand alone as an R01 and will be reviewed independently. If the R01 depends on multiproject core resources, include those resources and associated costs in the R01 budget. If both are fundable, you cannot withdraw from the multiproject award—be aware of this policy before committing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program topic: novelty and fit
rubrics_metrics.description: Demonstrate that the proposed program topic is novel or that prior work used inadequate methods; show knowledge of gaps, discrepancies, or roadblocks in the field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show the program has a central focus and coherent direction, with good synergy and integration among components. Explain why a multiproject coordinated approach is required or uniquely advantageous versus separate projects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Individual projects: preliminary data
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide sufficient preliminary data to support each project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give an account of published and unpublished results indicating progress, and summarize the importance of those findings in relation to the Specific Aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research plan quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Research Plans should be innovative, hypothesis-driven (where appropriate), well-developed, and create synergy among projects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plans must include sufficient details and focused experimental approaches, address potential problems, propose alternative approaches and contingency plans, consider difficulties and limitations, and explain procedures/materials that may be hazardous to personnel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance
rubrics_metrics.description: Fully articulate the significance of the proposed work and how it will move the field forward.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain the importance of the work for the team and the broader research area and how the program's outcomes will exert lasting impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biosketch completeness
rubrics_metrics.description: Include biosketches for all key personnel in the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each biosketch must include all required sections: personal statement, positions and honors, contribution to science, and research support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigators and institutional support
rubrics_metrics.description: Demonstrate that investigators have sufficient expertise and that the institution will provide the necessary support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain how the institution will support the work, confirm investigators are qualified and have enough time to devote, describe collaborators/consultants used to fill gaps, list adequate equipment/space/support staff, and include letters for any cofunding commitments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Individual cores must support multiple projects
rubrics_metrics.description: Each core must be described as supporting at least two projects and include administrative and technical details.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe the administrative infrastructure, roles and responsibilities of the core leader, detailed facilities/approaches/support offered, management structure and time commitments for coordination, plans for scientific meetings, prioritization of core services, and evidence of expertise to direct the core. Show how the core adds to the central focus of the program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program management and governance
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a clear plan for overall program coordination, governance, and organization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain overall program goals and significance, how studies will move the field forward, describe synergy among projects, define each PI's roles/responsibilities, governance and organizational structure, need for formal consortium agreements, confirm each PI leads a project, list sites and what each facility will do, describe coordination among sites, and plan for data management and coordination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cohesion and added value (synergy)
rubrics_metrics.description: Demonstrate how the multiproject program is cohesive and how the whole program is better than individual projects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pay special attention to synergy: describe how components will be coordinated to address overall goals, include a schematic overview of interactions and collaborations among projects and cores, indicate shared resources/publications/coauthorships, and give examples of tangible added value (e.g., shared reagents, populations, technologies, data tools).

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation, formatting, and organization
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure clear, concise writing and correct application formatting and organization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Label materials clearly so peer reviewers can find information, use an approved font, follow page limits, place items in the correct section, and avoid improper formatting or sloppy presentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Highlighting synergy in the Overview
rubrics_metrics.description: In the Overview section, explicitly highlight program synergy and coordination among components.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a schematic overview of interactions and collaborations, describe how projects and cores will coordinate to meet overall aims, and list collaborations and relevant coauthored publications among program members.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer review structure and emphasis
rubrics_metrics.description: A special emphasis panel evaluates the entire multiproject application, assessing the overall integrated program and each project/core component.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Peer reviewers will discuss the overall program using the five NIH standard review criteria and emphasize interaction, collaboration, programmatic themes, and synergy. They will consider project/core strengths and weaknesses in relation to the overall program and then discuss individual components.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scoring rules for multiproject applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Scoring differs by component: the overall program, research projects, and cores have specific scoring rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Overall program and each research project receive an overall impact score of 1 to 9. Research projects (except in investigator-initiated P01s) get criterion scores; cores do not (except investigator-initiated P01s where cores receive impact scores). For multiproject applications submitted to an RFA, cores may receive an overall impact score (1–9) or an Acceptable/Unacceptable rating. Applications are recommended for no further consideration if fewer than the required minimum number of meritorious research projects are present.

rubrics_metrics.name: Common pitfalls to avoid
rubrics_metrics.description: Common mistakes that weaken scores include lack of synergy, poor coordination, insufficient data or expertise, and presentation problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific pitfalls: low impact/weak project; lack of synergy/integration; lack of program coordination; lack of innovation; insufficient expertise or failure to use recruited expertise; insufficient preliminary data; failure to describe significance; insufficient experimental detail/unfocused approaches; lack of hypothesis-driven studies; lack of convincing rationale; failure to address pitfalls and alternative approaches; overcommitment of program director/project leaders; incomplete cores lacking facility/approach/project support descriptions; failure to demonstrate progress for renewals; failure to include a multi-PI plan; and improper formatting/sloppy presentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prepare for electronic submission via ASSIST
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit multiproject applications electronically using the NIH ASSIST system (not Grants.gov).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the same login and system requirements as Grants.gov and log in with eRA Commons credentials. ASSIST allows delegation of responsibilities, granting/denying access to application components, and integration with eRA Commons. Only authorized roles (Signing Official in eRA Commons or Authorized Organizational Representative in Grants.gov) may submit an application using ASSIST. For multiple PI applications, each PI must be registered in eRA Commons. Test the ASSIST environment, use annotated samples and eRA training materials, and submit well ahead of the due date to fix potential submission problems. NIH will not accept error corrections after submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: ASSIST form order and component organization
rubrics_metrics.description: ASSIST presents application components in a specific order and groups components of the same type together.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ASSIST puts an overall component describing the entire application first, then data summaries, then additional component types in alphabetical order, with components of the same type grouped in the order you create them. Use provided annotated multiproject application images and the test environment to become familiar with the interface.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration and institutional submission checks
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure institutional registrations and submission settings are correct before submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Register in eRA Commons and verify settings; if your institution uses its own submission software, confirm it submits multiproject data correctly to ASSIST. Submit early to allow time to fix problems like duplicated sections, omitted or misordered components, or unrecognized special characters. Confirm who in your organization can perform the submission and that required personnel (e.g., PIs) are registered.
